ledger.contains: Taiwan Ministry of Justice Anti-Corruption Informant Rewards and Protection Regulation (獎勵保護檢舉貪污瀆職辦法), text as amended 1 Feb 2019, 15 articles: covered offences; reward for reports made before discovery to prosecutors, judicial police or ethics units; exclusions (facts not matching the judgment, officials reporting in the course of duty, accomplices, bribe-givers, anonymous or false-name reports, reports by proxy); +50% when more than five offenders convicted, max NT$10 million; one case one reward, sharing rules; one third after conviction, rest when final; one tenth in special cases; tax deducted; heirs; recovery only for false accusation; MOJ review committee; written or oral reports with identity; confidentiality; protection; dedicated hotlines; transitional rule. Anonymous_filing and cap already in the data; added conviction requirement, partial payment, reduced and increased shares, tax and entitlement rules. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).
ledger.to_do: The reward schedule by sentence length (附表：貪污瀆職案件檢舉獎金給獎標準, PDF/DOC attachment) is not stored; download and extract the amounts per sentence band.

ledger.contains: CRA web page 'Report offshore tax cheating - Outcomes' (modified 2026-08-11): reward of 5-15% of federal tax collected (excluding penalties and interest) if at least $100,000 is collected; levels 5/7.5/10/12.5/15%; no upfront payments, partial payments possible after the threshold, payment only after objection and appeal rights expire; rewards taxable; grounds for ineligibility or contract termination; grievance panel; factor table (quality, relevance, cooperation, value). No statistics. The 5%, 15% and $100,000 rules were already recorded; this pass adds the discretionary rule (reward level set by the CRA from listed factors). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

OSC news release 6 Apr 2020: CAD 525,000 award to a company outsider; cumulative 'more than $8 million' awarded since July 2016; restates the up to $5 million award cap. Award (case c-3806e64152) and cumulative (o-4d6304a470) already recorded; the cap is boilerplate already recorded as a rule from the programme pages, not repeated as a rule row. Nothing added. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

OSC news release 20 Mar 2023: award of approximately $481,000 to an insider; cumulative $9.33 million awarded; tips have led to enforcement action against 19 respondents and approximately $48 million in monetary sanctions and voluntary payments; tips come in anonymously through counsel and from across Canada, the U.S. and abroad; up to $5 million cap; the OSC published its programme update on 9 March 2023. Already recorded: case c-af3cd21ca2, cumulative o-a3d82a11f1, sanctions o-d53cba0ae9. Added: 19 respondents (proposed indicator respondents_sanctioned) and the 9 March 2023 publication event. Cap and anonymous filing through counsel are boilerplate already recorded as rules from the programme pages. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

OSC web page 'Award eligibility and process' (2026): Policy 15-601 award criteria (over $1 million in sanctions and/or voluntary payments), voluntary and original information, ineligible information, 120-day window after internal reporting, individual eligibility (compliance/audit roles generally excluded), culpable, anonymous (through lawyers) and joint whistleblowers, timelines (paid after appeals expire), award amount 5-15% up to $5 million ($1.5M not contingent on collections, $1.5-5M contingent), discretion and factors, confidentiality, tax. No statistics. Five rules were already recorded from this page; added award cap $5M, non-contingent cap $1.5M and the $1M threshold. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

CMA press release (6 Jun 2023): cartel informant reward cap raised from £100,000 to £250,000; rewards discretionary, paid if information is significant and leads to enforcement; reward separate from leniency, normally not for leniency applicants unless their role was peripheral. Also general cartel sanctions (fines up to 10% of turnover, up to 5 years' prison, up to 15 years' director disqualification), which are not about the reward programme. The two cap rules and the rule-change event were already recorded; no statistics on rewards paid. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

CMA guidance 'Rewards for information about cartels' (first published 31 Mar 2014, current version states the £250,000 cap): why rewards are offered, what a cartel is, hotline, confidentiality, process (no-names first contact, identity then required), discretionary rewards set by value of information, harm stopped, effort and risk; paid only at the end of an investigation, expenses reimbursed; leniency applicants normally not rewarded; complainant businesses unlikely to get rewards. Cartel sanctions (10% of turnover, 5 years' prison, 15 years' disqualification) are not about the programme. No statistics. The £250,000 cap is already recorded from the 2023 news release (not duplicated); the discretionary rule was already recorded; this pass adds the anonymous-filing rule. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

GOV.UK guidance for the Strengthened Reward Scheme (26 Nov 2025): reward 15-30% of tax collected (excluding penalties and interest) when information leads to at least £1.5 million collected; discretionary; exclusions (civil servants, the taxpayer involved, information already known, illegal funding risk, legal duty, acting for others, second-hand from ineligible persons, anonymous reports); how to report (form character limits of 1,200 and 500 are not programme data); no feedback; years may pass before payment. All five rules and the launch event were already recorded; nothing further in scope. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Budget 2025 (HTML, whole document searched): para 3.3 mentions launching a strengthened informant reward scheme modelled on the US; section 5.9 'Rewards for informants of high-value tax fraud' says rewards up to 30% where over £1.5 million is recovered, with immediate effect (26 Nov 2025). These rules and the launch are already recorded from HMRC's guidance. Table 4.1 prints only the aggregate line 'HMRC: Further measures to close the tax gap' (+75m to +2,590m, 2025-26 to 2030-31), which covers many measures and is out of scope; the informant measure's own costing is in the policy costings document. Nothing new added. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Budget 2025 policy costings (128 pp.); only p. 104 'Rewards for informants of high value tax fraud' concerns the programme: measure description (over £1.5 million, up to 30%, effective 26 Nov 2025), tax base, behavioural-response costing, Exchequer impact 2025-26 to 2030-31 (+0, +0, +10, +55, +95, +65 £m; all six already recorded as exchequer_yield_forecast). The rest of the document costs other measures and is out of scope. Nothing new added. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Written question UIN 93208 (tabled 20 Nov 2025, answered 27 Nov 2025): the scheme launched 26 Nov 2025; reward 15-30% when information leads to more than £1.5M tax collected (rules already recorded from HMRC guidance); HMRC will keep publishing annual totals but not the number or size of rewards (already recorded as an event). Nothing new added. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

UK Anti-Corruption Strategy 2025 (121 pp., whole text searched). On rewards: commitment 1.1.3 (para 39.III, due 2026) to consider the Fisher review and assess financial incentive schemes for reporting economic crime (already recorded as an event); 1.1.4 (due 2027) reform whistleblowing in employment. Figures present but out of scope: SFO Intelligence Division about 1,450 referrals and 167 whistleblowing disclosures in 2024-25 (footnote 41; SFO has no reward programme), IACCC requests and assets, a Cardiff Council whistleblower-initiated bribery case (no reward). Nothing new added. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Ghana Whistleblower Act, 2006 (Act 720), assent 16 Oct 2006; stored copy (12 pp.) prints the arrangement of 32 sections but the text stops after s. 25 (ss. 26-32 on fund management, disbursement, accounts and audit, annual report, regulations and interpretation are missing from this copy). Contents: disclosable improprieties, who may disclose and to whom (18 recipients), procedure, confidentiality (offence: 500-1,000 penalty units or 2-4 years), forwarding to the Attorney-General within 7 working days, 60-day investigation, protection from victimisation, CHRAJ complaints and orders (incl. a reward from the Fund), legal aid, police protection, immunity, void gag clauses, Whistleblower Reward Fund (voluntary contributions and money voted by Parliament), reward on conviction, reward of 10% of money recovered or an amount set by the Attorney-General. No statistics. The 10% rule and assent event were already in the data; added entitlement, conviction route, investigation deadline and the confidentiality fine. Sections 26-32 cannot be extracted from this copy (they are absent, not unread). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

GVH web page (undated, current at 2026-10-05): 13 questions and answers on the informant reward under Tpvt. s. 79/A. Covers why rewards are paid; what a hardcore cartel is; which evidence qualifies (indispensable written evidence, or information enabling a court-authorised dawn raid that finds such evidence); who may inform (any natural person); exclusions (staff of a prior leniency applicant, evidence obtained by crime or petty offence, evidence split to multiply rewards, no fine imposed incl. cases taken over by the European Commission, breach of GVH-ordered cooperation); criminal-law context (Criminal Code s. 420: 1-5 years for bid-rigging cartels; immunity only for those reporting first to criminal authorities or under a corporate leniency application: out of scope); contact details (Detection Office, anonymous enquiry and Kartell Chat); procedure (anonymous prior enquiry; 5-day deadline to claim after notification; separate order if evidence unsuitable; preliminary assessments not binding); decision within 30 days of the closing decision and payment due 30 days after the order is final; amount 1% of all fines in the case, max HUF 50 million, free of personal income tax; not reclaimable if a court later cuts the fine unless the evidence proves unlawful through the informant's fault; one reward per person per case, separate rewards for separate people; informant may be heard as a witness and can ask for sealed identity data. No statistics. Anonymous filing of a reward claim is not provided (only anonymous enquiries; identity can be sealed), so no anonymous_filing row. Rules extracted: pct min/max, filing deadline, decision and payment deadlines, tax exemption, leniency-staff exclusion (cap already in data). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

GVH annual report to Parliament on 2010 (96 pp.): competition enforcement (cartels, abuse of dominance, mergers, consumer protection), fines, court review, advocacy, international work, budget and staff. Programme content only on PDF p. 7 (informant reward introduced 1 April 2010: 1% of fine, max HUF 50 million; about 20 private persons came forward vs 2-3 non-complainant signals a year before; 50% not cartel, 40% cartel but not meeting the law's requirements, 10% application admitted), p. 35 (reward mentioned as a detection tool) and p. 69 (press conference end of March 2010). Rule rows, launch event and tips_received 2010 were already in the data; added the three shares and the press-conference event. The 2-3 pre-reward signals a year are not a programme number (before launch) and are left out. Everything else (cartel fines e.g. HUF 9.6 bn in 2010, leniency applications 3) is out of scope. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

GVH annual report to Parliament on 2013 (148 pp.). Programme content: PDF p. 10 (2013 talks with about 25-30 potential applicants, one application admitted; first proceeding opened largely on an informant's information closed in 2013, Vj-43/2011 office supplies, eleven companies fined HUF 1,003.6 million, reward payable over HUF 10 million; others failed the indispensability test or withdrew from fear) and p. 53 (office-supplies cartel decided in December 2013; no further reward numbers); p. 7, 16, 19-20, 25 on the new Detection Office (set up 15 April 2013) without reward numbers; p. 101 decision table lists Vj-43/2011 with the HUF 1,003,600,000 fine. All in-scope rows (tips 25-30, 1 admitted, the case) were already in the data; nothing new to add. Rest of the report (other cases, fines, leniency, consumer protection, budget) out of scope. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

GVH annual report to Parliament on 2014 (122 pp.). Programme content: PDF p. 13 (informant enquiries rose again in 2014 after the 2013 dip; about 20 potential informant enquiries, 2 applications admitted; informant reward said to help detection more than leniency, of which none admitted in 2014) and p. 22 (calendar: 24 January 2014 press conference on the first cartel case with an informant reward payment). All three items were already in the data; nothing new. Rest (fines, other cases, consumer protection, budget) out of scope. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

English annual report of the ACRC for 2010 (104 pages). Programme content: corruption reports received by year 2002-2010 (total, corruption allegations, Code of Conduct violations, general grievances); reports handled by outcome; reports transferred to investigative agencies by year with investigation results and substantiation rates, by receiving agency and (for 2010) by sector and type; people indicted/reprimanded and money levied; insider whistle-blowing referrals; protection requests by year and type with outcomes; fines for identity-protection breaches; honours and award money for informants; reward applications, approvals, recovered amounts and reward money by year 2002-2010; and the legislative history of the Public Interest Whistleblower Protection bill (2008-2010). Rest of the report (ombudsman complaints, integrity assessments, corruption impact assessment, officials dismissed for corruption, subsidy inspections, Code of Conduct operation, education, administrative appeals) is out of scope. Reward-table total for recovered amount is misprinted ("21,954,733,31") and 2010 is printed "45,05,568,093" (already recorded as 4505568093); text gives "almost 22 billion won" (recorded). Bill milestones (submitted to National Assembly 29 Oct 2009, etc.) not recorded as events because the Act itself (2011) is already an event. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

English annual report of the ACRC for 2014 (96 pages). Programme content: corruption reports received by year 2002-2014; reports handled by disposal; referral totals (total row only) with results; people prosecuted/disciplined, warnings, institutional-improvement recommendations and KRW 553 billion to be recovered; referrals by agency; 2014 referrals by sector and type; internal whistleblowing referrals; protection rules and requests (2008-2014 and 2014) with outcomes; identity-protection fines; award and reward rules (restating the 2013 report: awards up to KRW 100 million, self-disclosure up to 20%/KRW 200 million, rewards 4-20% up to KRW 2 billion; not duplicated in the rules table) and cumulative payments; public-interest reports by sector and by year 2011-2014, handling and sanctions, protection requests, rewards by year and by sector, largest rewards; reward-rule changes in 2014 (minimum penalty, 10 payments a year); amendment bill; public awareness levels 2011-2014. Not recorded (context, not programme statistics): survey/inspection of 600 institutions and memo to 1,300; organisations with internal procedures (75 in 2013, 105 in 2014); education sessions and leaflets; text roundings identical to table values (KRW 397/227/28 million). The text says the Act took effect "Dec. 30, 2011" (misprint for 30 Sep 2011); the Jan. 14, 2014 revision on political-activity orders is mentioned without saying which Act, not recorded. Rest of the report (ombudsman, integrity, Corruption Inspection Team, dismissed officials, Code of Conduct, education, appeals) is out of scope. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

ACRC press release of 18 May 2017: rewards paid January-May 2017 (KRW 1.73088 billion to 332 reporters; split corruption 28 people / KRW 213.85 million and public interest 304 / KRW 1.51703 billion; KRW 10.2 billion recovered: amounts and the total of people already in the data, split by people added here), reward caps (KRW 3 billion corruption, KRW 2 billion public interest), record reward (KRW 1.1 billion in 2015, already a case from the 2015 report, not duplicated), five case summaries, and the April 2017 extension to private schools. Amounts read with 억 = 100,000,000 and 만 = 10,000. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

ACRC press release of 22 Sep 2026 (4 pages incl. an infographic): the Cabinet approves the three decree amendments (flat 30%, no cap; in force 29 Sep 2026 for applications filed afterwards); the event and the rules for the three laws are already in the data; added: the same change for Graft Act and Conflict of Interest Act reports (cap KRW 3 billion abolished, flat 30%). The infographic on p. 4 (image, OCR kor+eng) repeats the text (4-30% to 30%, 30억 cap abolished, five laws); no new numbers. Korean amounts: 억 = 100,000,000 and 만 = 10,000. A figure printed with 억 only is recorded in 억 (scale 'hundred million', e.g. 1.6억 = 1.6); one printed with 억 plus 천만/만 (e.g. 2억8천여만) is recorded in units of 만 원 (scale 'ten thousand': 2억8천만 = 28000), as earlier Korean rows do. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).
